claims.text: Coupling crystal plasticity with phase-field modeling can identify processing conditions that enhance phase stability.
Coupling crystal plasticity with phase-field modeling can identify processing conditions that refine alloy microstructures.
Coupling crystal plasticity with phase-field modeling can identify processing conditions that optimize alloy properties.
High-entropy alloys may be single-phase or multiphase solid solutions.
The proposed integrated framework can simulate severe high-strain mechanical processing and rapid thermal cycles.
High-strain processing promotes dynamic recrystallization.
Rapid thermal cycles and high-strain processing promote stress-induced phase transformations.
Dynamic recrystallization and phase transformations cause the evolution of grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
Crystal-plasticity simulation captures plastic deformation in the proposed alloy-processing regime.
Phase-field modeling predicts nucleation and growth processes in the proposed alloy-processing regime.
Coupling the two simulation methods enables control of microstructural scale.
Coupling the two simulation methods enables control of phase balance.
Control of microstructural scale and phase balance enhances physical and mechanical properties.
Processing conditions selected by the integrated model will produce greater phase stability than conventional processing.
Processing conditions selected by the integrated model will produce a finer grain structure than conventional processing.
The resulting microstructure will improve strength, ductility, or other targeted properties relative to conventional processing.
Conventional heat treatments and traditional thermomechanical routes do not concurrently control phase balance and microstructural scale.
The approach is applicable when dynamic recrystallization and phase transformations are the dominant mechanisms.
The approach may have limited predictive capacity outside regimes dominated by dynamic recrystallization and phase transformations.
Property improvements and optimal processing parameters require experimental calibration, and simulation-to-experiment extrapolation may introduce scaling uncertainty.
